exposure: low disease activity (SLE Disease Activity Index ≤4) for ≥12 months before conception
cohort: 54 women with diagnosed SLE at low disease activity for at least 12 months before conception and without anti-phospholipid antibodies, who had singleton pregnancies managed between 2005 and 2019
finding: A prednisone dose ≥10.5 mg/day and low CH50 complement activity in early pregnancy were identified as predictors of SLE flares during pregnancy in women previously considered low risk.
mod_finding: The flare group had a higher risk of emergent cesarean section compared to the non-flare group.
birth_weight: lower birth weight in the flare group
